description:
FILED s409 (Fable review of s408) by a probe; PRE-EXISTING at b7ce704 (verified in
a worktree) -- not #337's, but #337 makes the shape COMMON: `my sub` inside a sub
is exactly how post-5.26 code writes a private helper, and the enclosing sub's
parameters are what it reads.

    sub outer { my $x = shift; my sub inner { $x * 2 } return inner(); }
    print outer(3), " ", outer(4), "\n";
    perl: 6 8      PCL: unbound-variable $x__file__0 (CRASH at the first call)

The plain-named-sub twin crashes identically (perl there: 6 6, the first-instance
capture):

    sub outer { my $x = shift; sub inner { $x * 2 } return inner(); }

DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT (taken): the emission.  The promotion pass renames the
captured `my $x` to `$x__file__0` in BOTH subs -- but the declaration was lowered
by the raw-params optimisation, `(p-raw-params ($x__file__0) ...)`, which binds the
NAME LEXICALLY inside pl-outer and emits NO `(p-defcell $x__file__0 ...)`.  The
nested sub then reads a free `$x__file__0` -> unbound.  Compare `my $x = 70;` in
the same position: emits `(p-defcell $x__file__0 (make-p-box nil))` + `(p-scalar-=
$x__file__0 70)` and runs (140 140).  `my ($x) = @_;` in the same position is the
capture REFUSAL ("Parser2 TODO: lexical 'x' possibly captured by nested sub") --
loud.  So the three spellings of "take a param" go three ways: refusal / crash /
shared cell.  The nested sub must READ $x for the crash (`my sub inner { 7 }` +
`inner() + $x` is fine, probed).

FIX SHAPE: the promotion decision and the raw-params lowering must agree about
who owns the declaration.  Either (i) a promoted (`__file__N`) name is never a
raw-params binding -- the shift-lowering checks the promotion table and falls
back to the cell form (`p-defcell` + `p-scalar-=`), which lands the shape in the
registered "will not stay shared" family (shared cell: PCL 6 8 for the plain sub
where perl says 6 6, and 6 8 = perl for the `my sub` spelling), or (ii) the
raw-params param binding ALSO publishes the cell.  (i) is the smaller change and
its answer for `my sub` matches perl.  Guard rows: the two reproducers + the
`my $x = 70` twin (must not change) + `my ($x) = @_` (stays the refusal, or
joins (i)).  Bar: corpus-diff (emission changes for any file with the shape --
explain each), sweep TOTAL/LOST (a promotion change is scoping => the sweep IS
the gate).

Related: #347 (the family this joins), #337, #341 (op/lexsub.t sizing -- its
next blocker `undef-fn:main::pl-F` may be a cousin: measure).


DONE s410 (`d0f6236`), fix shape (i) as the task predicted, PLUS the
`my ($x) = @_` half, which the probe showed was worth joining: perl gives 6 8
there and PCL killed the whole FILE.  Its cause was separate and one line
long -- _scan_lex_facts only recorded a LIST declaration as a promotion
candidate when it declared TWO OR MORE names, so a one-element `my ($x) = ...`
was invisible to the promoter (it is not _single_scalar_decl's shape either,
being a list assignment, and the container branch wants a [@%] sigil).  The
N=1 case is the N=k case, cf. #267.  Seven shapes probed vs perl, all
identical.  The plain named-sub twin now RUNS (6 8 vs perl 6 6) and joins the
registered "will not stay shared" family in not-supported.md, where it is the
per-CALL member; it used to be a crash.
subject: CRASH: `sub outer { my $x = shift; my sub inner { $x } }` -- the promoted $x__file__0 is bound by p-raw-params (lexically) and no cell is emitted, so the nested sub reads an UNBOUND variable; `my $x = 70` in the same place works
